deep.reconstruction:
The page is very faint pencil. Almost nothing can be read with certainty, so any reconstruction has to lean on the neighbouring pages. The layout is visible: an indented block of formulas in the right half, one boxed expression at the top, a horizontal rule about two-thirds of the way down, two long lines of small script, and short lines at the bottom beginning roughly '1 + ...'. Taken together this matches the computation that runs from fol. 120r to fol. 121r. What follows is my identification of the setting. Only fragments of it are directly legible on this page.

Setting (from the neighbouring pages, in modern notation). Take Cartesian point (a,b,c), later renamed (x,y,z) on the next page. Define
  t(s) = s - s b^2/(s+α^2) - s c^2/(s+β^2),
so that
  t - a^2 = s(1 - a^2/s - b^2/(s+α^2) - c^2/(s+β^2)).
Thus t - a^2 = 0 is the equation of the confocal family of quadrics with squared semi-axes s, s+α^2, s+β^2. Its degenerate member s = 0 is the elliptic disc x = 0, y^2/α^2 + z^2/β^2 ≤ 1.
- σ (written b on fol. 120r) is the largest root of t - a^2 = 0, i.e. the ellipsoidal coordinate of the point.
- σ' (written b') is the largest root of t = 0.

Riemann studies the vector field
  X = ∫_σ^∞ sqrt(t-a^2) ds / (s sqrt((1+s/α^2)(1+s/β^2))),
  Y = -(ab/(α^2-β^2)) ∫_σ^∞ (s+β^2) dlog t / (sqrt(t-a^2) sqrt((1+s/α^2)(1+s/β^2))) + (const·π b/(α^2-β^2)) (σ'+β^2)/sqrt((1+σ'/α^2)(1+σ'/β^2)),
with Z obtained by symmetry (b↔c, α↔β).

The aim is to verify a divergence identity of the form ∂X/∂a + ∂Y/∂b + ∂Z/∂c = const·π (fol. 120r has -2π when b' = 0). The extra π-terms (Y', Z') coming from the root σ' have to be differentiated separately using implicit differentiation, (∂t/∂b')(∂b'/∂b) + ∂t/∂b = 0.

What this page appears to contain (my reading of the visible structure; uncertain):
(i) Top, right. A continuation of ∂Y/∂b obtained by differentiating under the integral sign and integrating by parts in s. The boxed fragment resembles the factor sqrt((1+s/β^2)/(1+s/α^2)) or its differential, and the following lines begin '+ ab/(α^2/β^2 - 1) ∫ ...' as on fol. 120r. The tools used are:
  d sqrt((1+s/β^2)/(1+s/α^2)) = ½ sqrt(...) (α^2-β^2)/((s+α^2)(s+β^2)) ds
  ∂t/∂b = -2bs/(s+α^2).
(ii) Middle. A line resembling 'Y' = ...' or '∂Y'/∂b = ...', i.e. the derivative of the boundary/π term through σ'. A further line involves ∂t/∂s at s = σ', which is needed for ∂σ'/∂b = -(∂t/∂b)/(∂t/∂s).
(iii) After the rule. A summed expression, apparently ∂Y/∂b + ∂Z/∂c = ... with terms b^2 s/(s+α^2)^2 and c^2 s/(s+β^2)^2. The two long small-script lines probably assemble ∂X/∂a + ∂Y/∂b + ∂Z/∂c.
(iv) Bottom. Short lines '√...' and '1 + ...', plausibly simplifying with the defining relation
  1 - a^2/σ - b^2/(σ+α^2) - c^2/(σ+β^2) = 0
to reach the constant.

All formulas above are inferred from context plus legible shapes. None of them is a confident transcription of this page.
errors: Nothing on this page can be checked for errors because it is essentially illegible.

Context, fol. 120r: ∂t/∂s is written there as -1 + b^2α^2/(s+α^2)^2 + c^2β^2/(s+β^2)^2. From t = s - s b^2/(s+α^2) - s c^2/(s+β^2) one gets ∂t/∂s = 1 - b^2α^2/(s+α^2)^2 - c^2β^2/(s+β^2)^2. Fol. 120r therefore has an overall sign slip, or it intends -∂t/∂s.

Context: the coefficient of the π-term in Y is π b/(α^2-β^2) on fol. 120r but 2π y/(α^2-β^2) on fol. 121r. Riemann evidently corrected the constant between the pages, and this page may contain the computation that forced the change.

results.what: Differentiation under the integral and integration by parts for integrals over confocal ellipsoidal parameter s, used to compute the divergence of a field defined by such integrals (field of an elliptic disc / degenerate ellipsoid)
results.modern_name: Ellipsoidal-coordinate (confocal quadric) integral representation of potentials; potential/field of an elliptic disc
results.usually_credited_to: Ivory, Jacobi, Dirichlet, Lamé (19th century); Riemann used this machinery in his 1861 fluid-ellipsoid paper

results.what: Implicit differentiation of the largest root σ' of t(s)=0 with respect to the coordinates
results.modern_name: Implicit function theorem / derivative of a root

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine potential-theory calculation in confocal ellipsoidal coordinates, of the kind Riemann used in his published 1861 work on fluid ellipsoids. The page is nearly illegible and shows no sign of a non-standard result.
